verses.mystical_translation: The king who measures timber first measures devotion — a nation’s labor girds a place for encounter.
Numbers organize hands and make a chorus of toil beneath the rock of the sacred place.
Old alliances extend the scaffold: wood and memory travel together across sea.
A place is framed so the rhythms of offering may give time to the people and the name.
Magnitude points beyond stone to the claim that the unseen exceeds every rival.
The paradox: a temple both encloses and confesses the uncontainable.
Skill in many crafts becomes prayer in thread, metal, and pigment.
Trees from the mountain become the ribs of a sanctuary; labor crosses borders.
Abundance of wood mirrors the intended wonder; grandeur and labor are yoked.
Provision becomes contract: grain, wine, and oil mark the wage of those who fell the cedar.
The sea-king reads the divine politics: kingship as a providential act acknowledged across coasts.
Praise bridges cultures: maker of cosmos acknowledged, wisdom invoked as the basis for building.
A craftsman arrives as carrier of family craft and cross-cultural technique.
A mixed-lineage artisan composes in metal, dye, and incision—craft as common speech between peoples.
Logistics acknowledged: sustenance follows the contract of craft.
Rafts become the slow liturgy of transport; sea and shore join to raise a house for the name.
Strangers counted become the workforce registry; the margin of the nation recorded in numbers.
Ranks and roles distribute the people into bearing, hewing, and supervising—order made of flesh and stone.

contemplative_note: Work and craft for sacred space interweave politics, labor, and devotion—attend to both human cost and liturgical intent.
safety_note: Contains material about forced labor and allocation of provisions; presented descriptively without endorsement.
